summary.text: 找 commonly means “look for” or “seek.” Its construction is disputed: a proposed explanation connects the spoken word to the word also written 抓 because their proposed Old Chinese forms are similar, but the borrowing is unproven.

formation.text: The graph’s construction remains disputed. One analysis gives 扌 a hand-related meaning and 戈 a sound role, but the cited Old Chinese readings do not form a straightforward sound match. A separate proposal is that similar-sounding words led the graph 找 to be reused for the word also written 抓; this remains unproven, and does not explain how “grasp” developed into “seek.” The older use of 找 as an alternate spelling of 划 for boat-poling does not establish the origin of the later seeking sense. The familiar scene of searching with a spear in hand is a mnemonic, not an established origin.

components.text: 扌 is the positional form of 手 (“hand”). One proposed analysis assigns it a hand-related meaning in 找, but that role is disputed; the hand radical is also reported in the separate boat-poling use.
One proposal assigns 戈 a sound role in 找. 戈 independently depicts an ancient weapon, but that object history does not establish a phonetic function here.

sound_limitation.text: The cited Zhengzhang Old Chinese values for 戈 and 找 do not give a straightforward sound match. Their different modern Mandarin readings likewise do not settle every possible historical analysis.

sound.text: The cited Zhengzhang reconstructions differ and do not provide a straightforward sound match.
In current Standard Mandarin, the component and host have different readings; this comparison does not establish their historical relationship.

history.text: 找 is recorded as an alternate spelling of 划 for “propel a boat with a pole,” with Song-era rhyme-dictionary material cited for this shared use. This does not establish that the seeking sense developed from boat-poling or that 划 was a graphic ancestor of 找.

A separate proposal is that similar-sounding words led 找 to be reused for the spoken word also written 抓, “grasp.” If so, this would be reuse of a written sign for another word, not a change in the sign’s meaning. The borrowing, early use of either word, and a semantic path from grasping to seeking are not established.
The selected seal-script-style image is a modern vector redraw showing 戈 alone, not an early form of 找. No early glyph sequence for 找 is established; the character is not recorded in Shuowen.

uncertainties.text: The proposed phonetic role for 戈 conflicts with the cited Old Chinese values for 戈 and 找. The separate proposal compares 找 with 抓 but does not establish borrowing or a semantic path from “grasp” to “seek.”

The historical dictionary places seeking, returning change, and making up a deficiency broadly from the Ming period onward, but does not date their first examples or establish their order of development.
The weapon depicted by 戈 has no independently established name here that supports a proposal that its object-name was borrowed to write 找.

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The dictionary identifies 找 as an alternate form of 划 in the sense “propel a boat with a pole” (讀 huá). It cites Song-era rhyme-dictionary entries, including Jiyun, for 划/找 in that sense. It distinguishes this from 找 meaning “seek,” “return change,” or “make up a deficiency,” which it says became current as separate senses from the Ming period onward (讀 zhǎo). This supports a historical homographic/variant use and a later sense distinction; it does not specify a dated first Ming example.

evidence.text: The entry reports that Jiyun says 划/找 may be written with the hand radical in the boat-poling sense. It also summarizes earlier distinct senses of 划: boat propulsion, cutting/harvesting, and sickle. evidence.text: This entry proposes a phono-semantic analysis of 找, with 扌 semantic and 戈 phonetic, and gives 戈 as Old Chinese *koːl. It separately says 找 was originally a variant of 划 and proposes the modern “seek” word derives from 抓, citing Middle Chinese tsraewX and Zhengzhang (2003). The page itself flags the variant/划 claim as needing a source. These are source assertions, not independently established here; the MOE dictionary supports the older 划/找 relationship but does not establish 戈 as a sound component for the later zhǎo word.

These distinct systems make a possible sound association with the Zhengzhang form proposed for 找 visible, but do not by themselves establish borrowing, an early source-word use, or a semantic transition from grasping to seeking.
evidence.title: 抓 - Wiktionary

evidence.text: The page gives modern Beijing Pinyin gē and Middle Chinese kwa, and lists Zhengzhang 2003 Old Chinese *koːl versus Baxter–Sagart 2014 system 1.1 *kʷˤaj. These are the page’s character-specific values, separate from the proposed 找 and 抓 readings. The contrast with the proposed 找 *ʔsruːʔ makes the 戈-as-phonetic proposal especially unsupported by this comparison; it does not rule out all possible historical analyses.
evidence.title: 戈 - Wiktionary

evidence.text: The entry describes 戈 as shaped after an ancient weapon, with blade, shaft, and other parts; it says the oracle-bone form’s vertical stroke represents the long shaft. This supports an independent object-form account for 戈, but gives no evidence that the name of that weapon was borrowed to write 找 or that 戈 is a phonetic in the later seeking sense.
evidence.title: 漢字「戈」：字形演變

evidence.field: File summary and original file link
evidence.text: The exact File page identifies 戈-seal.svg as a modern vector depiction of 戈 in Shuowen seal-script style, credits the character data to sources including Academia Sinica and Chinese Etymology, and links the original SVG at https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/8b/%E6%88%88-seal.svg. Its reuse note refers to Richard Sears permission; the associated Commons agreement says the images are free to use for any purpose under stated licensing, and Commons describes this vector representation as public domain. This is a redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph.
evidence.title: File:戈-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.text: The Commons agreement records copyright-holder approval for publication and states that the images may be used by anyone for any purpose subject to the licensing requirements. It also distinguishes images from the database schema and methods of organizing images. This supports reuse of the selected individual Commons image, not bulk reuse of its source database.
evidence.title: Commons:Ancient Chinese characters/Richard Sears Agreement

evidence.text: The database notice reserves rights in site content and permits personal noncommercial browsing/use absent a separate agreement; it does not grant general reuse permission for images. Accordingly, the Sinica character page is cited for its account, not selected as a glyph asset.

evidence.field: A01513 找, character notes and cited examples
evidence.text: The entry says 找 is not recorded in Shuowen and describes its visible form as left 扌 and right 戈. It lists seeking and monetary adjustment senses under zhǎo, and cites textual examples including 儿女英雄传 chapter 9, 红楼梦 chapter 31, 俗书刊误 volume 11, and 警世通言 volume 11. The page supplies no dates for the cited editions, so these references do not independently establish a precise first-use date.
evidence.title: [A01513] 找 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry treats 找 as an alternate form of 划 when 划 means propelling a boat with a pole. It cites Jiyun’s entry for 划/找 in that sense and distinguishes the separate 找尋, 找還, and 補不足 senses as usages current from the Ming onward, read zhǎo. It also reports that earlier dictionaries describe 划 with separate boat-propulsion, cutting/harvesting, and sickle senses. The entry supports a historical shared use, not a graphic ancestry from 划 to 找, and gives no dated first Ming example.
evidence.title: [A00337-001] 找 (划) - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.field: Chinese glyph origin and Old Chinese comparison
evidence.text: The page lists a Zhengzhang (2003) Old Chinese series under 爪: 抓 *ʔsruː, *ʔsruːʔ, *ʔsruːs; 爪 *ʔsruːʔ; 笊 *ʔsruːʔ, *ʔsruːs; 找 *ʔsruːʔ. It separately calls 扌 semantic and 戈 phonetic, assigning 戈 *koːl. These are incompatible proposals as presented on the page: the cited 找 value aligns with the 爪-series values, not the listed 戈 value. The page’s statement that the common sense was borrowed from 抓 is a proposal, not independently established evidence of borrowing.
evidence.title: 找 - Wiktionary

evidence.text: Wiktionary proposes that 找 was originally a variant form of 划 and that the later word was borrowed from 抓, also listing Middle Chinese tsraewX for 抓. Its variant-of-划 statement is marked as needing a source on that page. The inspected MOE dictionary independently supports an older 找/划 shared spelling for boat-poling, but neither source establishes that this was the graphic origin of 找.
evidence.title: 找 - Wiktionary

evidence.field: Chinese glyph origin, Old Chinese readings
evidence.text: The page gives 找 *ʔsruːʔ and 戈 *koːl under its Zhengzhang values, while giving 抓 *ʔsruː, *ʔsruːʔ, *ʔsruːs. This suggests possible similarity between the proposed spoken forms of 找 and 抓, but does not document early use of both words, borrowing, or a semantic link between “grasp” and “seek.” It does not identify an original weapon name underlying a whole-graph loan.

evidence.text: The entry lists 找 *ʔsruːʔ in a 爪 phonetic series, while its separate phono-semantic analysis calls 扌 semantic and 戈 phonetic and gives 戈 *koːl. Those displayed values do not match as a straightforward phonetic pair. The sound analysis is a secondary proposal, not independent confirmation of 戈’s role.

evidence.field: Grasp entry, Old Chinese and Middle Chinese readings
evidence.text: For 抓 “grasp,” the entry gives Zhengzhang Old Chinese variants *ʔsruː, *ʔsruːʔ, and *ʔsruːs, alongside distinct Middle Chinese readings. Compared with the same source’s 找 *ʔsruːʔ, this offers a possible sound basis for the proposed borrowing, but does not establish that borrowing, an early dated use of either word, or a semantic path from grasping to seeking. The page also lists Baxter–Sagart system 1.1 values separately; those notations should not be merged with Zhengzhang’s.

evidence.text: The entry lists zhǎo for current Standard Mandarin and gives separate senses including “look for/seek,” giving change, and making up a deficiency. editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

search_audit.outcome: Opened the character-specific pages and inspected their current Mandarin readings, Zhengzhang series and proposed borrowing account. The proposed borrowing remains unsupported by a dated primary attestation or demonstrated semantic path.

gaps: The MOE dictionary dates the distinct zhǎo senses broadly to the Ming period but this research did not verify the earliest dated primary-text attestation or date the transitions among seeking, returning change, and making up a deficiency. The Ming-period claim remains dictionary analysis, not an independently checked earliest-use citation.

No inspected paleographic source establishes the early graphic sequence for 找 itself. The MOE page notes that several listed oracle-bone, bronze, and manuscript resources are unavailable there; no claim is made that the presently visible graph has a verified ancient form.

The claim that 戈 is a phonetic component in the later 找 meaning “seek” conflicts with the proposed Zhengzhang sound set: Wiktionary gives 找 *ʔsruːʔ but assigns 戈 *koːl, and labels the phonetic-series analysis separately from the proposed borrowing from 抓. The source of the later word and the graphic history of the earlier 找~划 form should remain distinct pending stronger evidence.

The dossier’s local Baxter–Sagart table was checked: 戈 is listed as *kʷˤaj, 划 has *C.[g]ʷˤraj (?), and 抓 has *[ts](ˤ)ru and *tsˤ<r>uʔ; no 找 row was found. These are Baxter–Sagart table readings, distinct from the Zhengzhang notation cited above. The local rows are not emitted as external evidence because the requested character-specific official Unicode pages could not be verified.

The local Unihan_Readings.txt rows inspected give kMandarin 找 zhǎo (row 80154), 戈 gē (row 78919), and 划 huà (row 40318); the checked file search returned no row for 扌. These local readings are not evidence for an ancient phonetic relation. The required official Unicode character-specific click-through pages could not be opened, so these local values are recorded as a verification limitation, not external evidence.

The reported loan proposal from 抓 still lacks a primary source documenting both the early source-word sense and the later 找 sense, their actual early pronunciations, and the semantic path. The proposed sounds do not establish an object name for 戈; the weapon’s pictured referent is independently described by Academia Sinica, but its name is not shown to be the basis of the proposed borrowing.
No verified reuse terms or licensing statement for the repeated character-specific dictionary material were located; no local extract is recommended.

No inspected paleographic source supplies an early form sequence for 找 itself. The MOE dictionary says Shuowen does not record 找; its listed textual references include earlier rhyme-dictionary material for the boat-poling variant and later literary examples, but the research did not verify exact dated editions or a first occurrence.

The separate sense history is not fully established: the MOE dictionary broadly places seeking, change-returning, and deficiency senses from the Ming onward, but does not date the individual semantic transitions or independently verify a first Ming attestation.

The sound/loan claims remain uncertain. The Zhengzhang comparison has 找 *ʔsruːʔ and 抓 *ʔsruːʔ alongside differing readings, which offers a possible sound basis for a spoken-word borrowing; the evidence inspected does not establish early use of each word, actual borrowing, or the semantic development from “grasp” to “seek.” The separately proposed 戈 phonetic analysis conflicts with these values and with 戈 *koːl. An independently recoverable name for the pictured weapon was not established; the weapon’s depiction alone cannot ground a whole-graph loan claim.

The exact local Unihan rows supplied in the input give current kMandarin 找 zhǎo, 戈 gē, and 抓 zhuā. The local Baxter–Sagart table gives 戈 *kʷˤaj and 抓 *[ts](ˤ)ru / *tsˤ<r>uʔ, with no 找 row in the supplied data. These are local values, not external evidence; official Unicode character-specific record URLs were attempted but inaccessible, so no external Unihan click-through evidence is claimed. Local-file row locators were not provided for all supplied rows.

The Ministry dictionary’s separate 找 entry and its A00337-001 variant analysis were searchable and inspected as records for the appropriate graph and use; they do not provide an ancient graphic development sequence. The Academia Sinica 戈 page states All Rights Reserved, so it is used as linked evidence only. No broad dictionary extract is recommended because reuse permission and repeatable-extract value were not established.
No verified paleographic sequence for 找 itself was found. The MOE entry says Shuowen does not record 找, while its early-form reference list includes materials unavailable on the page.

The MOE dictionary dates the separate seek/change/deficiency senses broadly to the Ming period onward, but the reviewed material does not provide an independently checked earliest dated attestation or establish the order and semantic connections among those senses.
The 找~划 relationship is supported as a shared spelling/use for boat-poling; evidence inspected does not establish that 划 was a graphic ancestor of 找.

The proposed 抓-to-找 borrowing lacks primary evidence here for early attestations of both words, a documented semantic path, and the borrowing itself. Possible sound similarity in one reconstruction is insufficient to establish it.

The separate 扌-semantic/戈-phonetic account conflicts with the displayed Zhengzhang readings. It remains uncertain whether this reflects a mistaken assignment or another historical analysis; the source pages do not resolve it.

The local kMandarin rows and Baxter–Sagart rows supplied in the input were not promoted to external evidence. Exact official Unihan character pages could not be inspected, and the Baxter–Sagart table is local data rather than an inspected external page.

The local Unihan_Readings.txt rows inspected list kMandarin 戈 gē (row 78919), 手 shǒu (row 79662), 扌 shou without a tone mark (row 79673), and 找 zhǎo (row 80154). These local values are not external evidence; the official Unicode character-specific pages were inaccessible. Externally opened dictionary pages independently give modern Mandarin gē, zhǎo, and shǒu, but do not replace the requested official Unihan click-through verification.

The local Baxter–Sagart table was checked: 戈 is *kʷˤaj (MC kwa), 手 is *n̥uʔ (MC syuwX), and 抓 has *[ts](ˤ)ru and *tsˤ<r>uʔ (MC tsraew and tsraewX); no row for 找 or 扌 was found. These are local Baxter–Sagart 2014 table values, distinct from the Zhengzhang reconstructions. The opened secondary page’s Baxter–Sagart values for 抓 agree in substance, but there is no externally inspected character-specific Baxter–Sagart value for 找 in this research.

No primary source inspected establishes the proposed borrowing of the spoken word also written 抓 by 找, the early dated senses and pronunciations of both words, or a semantic link from “grasp” to “seek.” Their Zhengzhang values offer a possible sound comparison only. The weapon depicted by 戈 has no independently established object name here that would support a separate object-name loan proposal.

The MOE dictionary supports a historical 找/划 shared spelling for boat-poling and broadly places separate seek, change-returning, and deficiency senses from the Ming period onward. It does not establish that 划 was a graphic ancestor of 找, date the first Ming use, or demonstrate the order and semantic links among those later senses.
No early paleographic sequence for 找 was verified. The MOE entry says 找 is not recorded in Shuowen and marks several early-form reference materials unavailable on its page.

The existing 戈-seal glyph remains the selected visual candidate; it illustrates the component’s independent object history and is not an early form of 找. The additional 手-seal page is provenance-verified, but its direct image request returned a cache miss; it is not selected. No broad dictionary extract is recommended because reuse permission and editorial value for a repeatable local extract were not established.
